pass_a_gloss: [...] through the lyre of the one who sings psalms, saying thus: I will open in parables my mouth, I will utter things hidden from foundation of world. And he was speaking to the Jews too in parables. So they did not give counsel to the people, he says, but neither did it know the one deep-voiced. And they did not give counsel so as that a despised people should not hear. For if they had been giving counsel, a despised people would not have been called [so]; but rather blessed, as having recognized the Redeemer. But there was not, he says, understanding to the one hearing. For the Jews, being without understanding, were not testing the voices of the leaders, nor discerning whether ever they counsel good things or do the opposite. [Lemma, Isaiah 33:20-21:] Behold Zion the city, our salvation, your eyes will see Jerusalem, a rich city, tents which will not be shaken, the pegs of its tent for the age of time, nor will its cords be broken, because the name of the Lord is great to you. A place will be for you, rivers and canals broad and spacious. The words of God having been placed through the middle, which he made toward the senseless scribes of the Jews and those counselling unholy things, the person of the lovers of the truth is brought in again, of those both having recognized the appearing of Christ and saying [Behold Zion]: either the Church on earth, or the fair city above in heavens, the nurse of the saints. So that whether someone should name the Church on earth, or should receive into mind that one, one will be the thing shown through both. For those who have come to be in the one below will be in due times also in that one above and in heavens. So since, from much great joy all but, they even leap up, having recognized Zion, in which is our salvation, that is, Christ, pointing it out to one another, at once the divine word takes over the voices from them, and says: Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a rich city; and he speaks as from likeness of the ancient tent, the one in the desert. And he names Zion rich, and that the tent will be unshaken. For he insists that it has unbreakable cords, and pegs fixed continually. For the Church has been firmly set, and has an unshakable abiding toward well-being: For gates of Hades, it says, will not prevail against it. And he gives the cause through which it will be such, and says to those who believed in Christ that the name of the Lord is great to you. For to those who did not admit the faith, the name of Christ is not great and glorified. But among us who believed, great and lofty. For we worship [him] as God, as truly Son of the Father, as Word become man for salvation of all. This then, he says, the tent always abiding, a place [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: …through the lyre of the psalmist, saying: “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden from the foundation of the world” (Psalm 78:2; Matthew 13:35). And He spoke to the Jews too in parables.

So they did not give counsel to the people, he says, nor did the people know Him whose speech is deep. Nor did they give the counsel that would have kept the people from being called a despised people. For if they had given counsel, the people would not have been called despised; they would rather have been called blessed, as those who had recognized the Redeemer. But there was, he says, no understanding in the one who heard (Isaiah 33:19). For the Jews, being without understanding, did not test the voices of their leaders, nor discern whether they were giving good counsel or doing the opposite.

“Behold Zion, the city, our salvation! Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a rich city, tents that will not be shaken; the pegs of its tent stand for ever, nor will its cords be broken, because the name of the Lord is great to you. You will have a place, rivers and canals, broad and spacious” (Isaiah 33:20-21).

Between these come the words which God addressed to the senseless scribes of the Jews and to those who gave unholy counsel. Now the voice of the lovers of truth is brought in again, of those who have recognized the appearing of Christ and who say “Behold Zion,” meaning either the Church on earth or the fair city above in the heavens, the nurse of the saints. So whether one names the Church on earth or has that other city in mind, the thing shown by both will be one. For those who have been in the Church below will in due time be also in that city above, in the heavens.

Since, then, they all but leap for great joy at having recognized Zion, in which is our salvation, that is, Christ, and point it out to one another, at once the divine word takes up their words and says: “Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a rich city.” He speaks as if by likeness to the ancient tent in the wilderness. He calls Zion rich and says that the tent will be unshaken; for he declares that it has cords that cannot be broken and pegs fixed for ever. For the Church has been firmly set, and its continuance in well-being cannot be moved: “for the gates of Hades,” he says, “will not prevail against it” (Matthew 16:18).

And He gives the reason why it will be such, saying to those who have believed in Christ: “because the name of the Lord is great to you.” For to those who have not accepted the faith the name of Christ is not great and glorified; but with us who have believed it is great and exalted. For we worship Him as God, as truly the Son of the Father, as the Word made man for the salvation of all. This then, he says, the tent that abides for ever, is a place…

choices.english: the people would not have been called despised
choices.why: ἀκούω here 'to be called'; the sentence is counterfactual, not a free-standing beatitude.
Septuagint Isaiah 33:19; Cyril applies it to Christ speaking in parables.
The heavenly Jerusalem, nurse of the saints.
ἐρείδω, to fix firmly; said of the Church against the gates of Hades.
